07 November 2011 
• 
The complex traded bullish again after a major dip 
in all metals at the beginning of the month owing to 
uncertainty over the actions of the Greek govern-
ment. Bullish US Auto figures helped pgms, and the 
cut in ECB rates, combined with the impression that 
QEIII was on the slipway and being given a fresh 
coat of paint, added to the positive gold outlook. 
 
• 
Investor interest grew on the long side for gold by 
1.40 million tozs on COMEX.  Platinum saw decent 
NYMEX buying, but that was largely offset by sell-
ing from TOCOM as the drop in the Yen gave Japa-
nese investors a chance to take some profit on 
Platinum. Palladium saw a 3 % rise in investor 
longs overall. 
 
• 
ETF holdings grew for gold, silver and platinum, but 
went sideways for palladium in the week to the 28th 
of October.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
07 November 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
Gold has had a positive week with a dip to the 
lows on December COMEX of $1681 being fero-
ciously bid back up during the 1st of November 
and a close of $1756.10 on Friday. If gold could-
n’t do well during a week in which the Euro-zone 
rescue plans fell apart spectacularly of course, 
then there would be no hope. The implosion 
within the Greek government and the subsequent 
uncertainty over the success of the rescue pack-
age—a fairly generous affair—should help keep 
gold in the forefront, even in ‘risk off’ scenarios. 
 
 
• 
In the gold market, investor interest rose by 1.25 
million trozs, with COMEX positions adding 1.40 
million. The TOCOM liquidation was partly in con-
nection with the drop in the JPY as the Bank of 
Japan intervened aggressively in the FX market. 
This was a healthy  increase and represents al-
most 3 million tozs restored after the late August 
flush. 
 
 
• 
Gold ETF holdings increased by about 478,000 
Troy ounces in the week to the 4th of November, 
rising to 68.253 million ounces. The key gains 
were in ZKB holdings—perhaps reflecting the 
European epicentre of investor anxierty this past 
month.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
07 November 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Silver ETF Investment, Jan 07—November 11 
• 
Silver had a volatile week with the major trend still 
against the metal, and clear signs that US$34.80-
90 (December futures) is a difficult price level to 
break through. We tried top break there twice n 
Thursday and Friday with no success...Silver is in 
the difficult position of benefitting from a rally in 
gold, but suffering from the economic uncertainty 
arising from Euro zone economic woes. 
 
 
• 
Investor interest dipped slightly during the week 
to 1st November, suggesting that the previous 
weeks rally saw some profit-taking, perhaps un-
surprisingly after a fortnight of fairly horrible trend-
less movement. Small specs on COMEX liqui-
dated the most, with a decline in open interest of 
over 9 million Troy Ounces. 
 
• 
ETF positioning increased aggressively by around 
16 million Troy Ounces to the 4th of November, 
helping to buoy the price during the latter part of 
the week.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
07 November 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• 
The Platinum price had a horribly volatile week as 
the market digested the implications of a Greek 
referendum and the possibility of a rapid default, 
with all the possibilities of a sharp contraction n 
bank lending and consumer sentiment that might 
arise from that. On the dip to $1563 (basis Jan NY-
MEX Platinum) the reality of mine cash costs and 
some decent auto sales numbers re-asserted them-
selves. US vehicle sales came in at 13.30 Million 
Units, the strongest in four years, and a rise of 7.50 
pct compared with October 2010, with decent sales 
noted in pick-up and SUV sales. 
 
  
• 
NYMEX platinum positions dropped grew by 51,000 
tozs over the week, handsomely reversing the mid-
October liquidation. The drop in the JPY, as the 
Bank of Japan intervened through the beginning of 
the week, led to a substantial liquidation of platinum 
longs, with 38,000 Troy ounces of selling.  
 
• 
Platinum ETF holdings rose by 10,000 Troy ounces 
during the week—with the principal growth coming 
from the ZKB fund, in a further vote of confidence in 
Platinum’s outlook, perhaps pinning more weight in 
a US recovery despite the dangers from Europe.

Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 
 
07 November 2011 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Palladium Exchange Investment, Apr 09—October 11 
Palladium ETF Investment, Apr 07—October 11 
• 
The week ending the 28th October ended with a 
pronounced dragonfly doji pattern, which gave warn-
ing of a reversal  in the short term trend—mentioned 
during last Monday’s report. That chart signal 
proved good to its word and Palladium dropped to a 
low of $624 dollars basis December futures on NY-
MEX. Since then the market has digested decent 
US auto sales and a generally buoyant precious 
complex, and we made a weekly high of $674.50. 
The price is however constrained by some pressure 
from two directions for investors. One is the long 
term support that we saw at $695 levels. That may 
now work as resistance. Secondly, we are bumping 
up against the daily Ichimoku cloud. Overall how-
ever, the metals performance looks capable of an 
assault on the important $695 level assuming we do 
not get another wave of ‘risk off’ activity. 
 
• 
Investors added to longs and appeared to see some 
short covering as well during the week to the 1st of 
November, possibly on the large dip. 
 
• 
The ETFs were as good as flat during the week with  
only a shuffling of positions between the different 
funds being of note. Please note that I (NF) made 
an error on the ETFS (US) last week and overstated 
the metal held in the ETF by around 20,000 Tozs. 
Apologies for any confusion caused by that.
